first_impression.reaction: The intro says out loud what I already think: "almost everything written about them comes from someone selling one side." Then "We sell neither." OK, so what do you sell? I went straight to the FAQ like I always do. It was short, sourced and didn't try to sell me a stone, so I went back up and read the grading, FTC and ACCC sections properly. This is one of the few lab-grown pages I've seen that doesn't read like a jeweller's ad.

journey.reaction: Good, that's the first thing I'd ask. But the obvious follow-up is: then how do you make money from this page? It's answered further down by the Advisor pitch, which is fine, but don't make me hunt.

journey.quote: The US Federal Trade Commission defines a diamond as a mineral of essentially pure carbon crystallised in the isometric system, with a hardness of 10, a specific gravity of about 3.52 and a refractive index of 2.42.
journey.reaction: Numbers and a named regulator. That's what I want. I can check this against the source in two minutes.

journey.quote: Here is how they compare, without prices.
journey.reaction: "Offered at a reduced price point" and "Higher for a comparable stone" tell me nothing. Is it 20% cheaper or 80%? I get why you won't quote prices, but even a sourced range or 'ask for both quotes on the same spec' would help. This is the one row I actually came for.

journey.quote: A GIA "Premium" stone and a stone graded elsewhere on colour and clarity scales are not described on the same terms, so ask which lab and which document type before comparing quotes.
journey.reaction: This is genuinely useful and I didn't know it. That's exactly the kind of catch that trips up a side-by-side quote comparison. Dates on the GIA change (June 2025, 1 October 2025) make it feel current.

journey.quote: As at October 2026, we found no ACCC guidance specific to lab-grown diamonds; the general rules on false or misleading claims apply.
journey.reaction: Honest about a gap instead of pretending there's an Australian rule. Saying 'we found none' with a date is what earns trust from me.

journey.section: Do lab-grown diamonds hold their value?
journey.quote: How either kind of stone holds its value over time is a separate question, and neither should be bought as an investment.
journey.reaction: Fair, and the buy-back questions are practical. But it reads a bit like a dodge. Everyone on Reddit says lab-grown resale is close to nothing. If you have no source, say you have no source; if there is one, cite it.

journey.quote: Neither option is automatically the more ethical one.
journey.reaction: Good. Using the FTC letters to show 'eco-friendly' claims are shaky is the kind of thing I'd screenshot. Kimberley Process line says it "has aimed to" rather than claiming it works, which is honest.

journey.section: From the ring to the destination
journey.quote: When you are ready, your Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments as your one point of contact, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Fee agreed in writing is a start. Still doesn't say whether you take a cut from venues or vendors. The jump from diamonds to destination weddings is a bit abrupt but at least it comes after the evidence.

journey.quote: The right stone is the one you can explain with a clear conscience and real pleasure, whichever it turns out to be.
journey.reaction: Bit of greeting-card wording to finish on after a page of facts. Harmless, I'd skip it.

unanswered_questions: Roughly how much cheaper is lab-grown than natural for the same size and quality, with a source and date?
Is there any data on resale or buy-back values for lab-grown stones, or is there genuinely none?
How does a GIA 'Premium' lab-grown stone compare in practice to an IGI report with colour and clarity grades?
Does Wedded Wonderland take commissions or referral fees from jewellers, venues or vendors?

turn_offs_found.quote: Relative cost | Offered at a reduced price point | Higher for a comparable stone
turn_offs_found.why: Vague where I wanted a number. Price is the main reason most people look at lab-grown.

turn_offs_found.quote: The right stone is the one you can explain with a clear conscience and real pleasure, whichever it turns out to be.
turn_offs_found.why: Emotional sign-off instead of a fact. Minor.

would_share_with: My fiancee, for the paperwork checklist and the GIA Premium/Standard point before we compare quotes
A mate weighing lab-grown, for the FTC naming and eco-claims sections

cta_reaction.quote: You can talk to a Wedded Concierge about a proposal or wedding abroad.
cta_reaction.why: It's placed after the evidence, which I respect, and it's not pushy. I'm here about a ring, not a planner, so I wouldn't click today. If I was already shortlisting planners I'd click only to ask about fees and commissions.

top_3_changes: Give the cost row something concrete: a sourced, dated indication of the price gap, or a clear instruction to get both quotes on the same spec and lab.
In the value section, either cite resale or buy-back evidence or state plainly that no reliable data was found as at October 2026.
Swap the closing 'clear conscience and real pleasure' line for one practical sentence (e.g. the three paperwork checks) and keep the Advisor mention factual.
